data.title: Cisco, OpenAI Launch Project to Safeguard Agentic AI
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Cisco Systems and OpenAI launched an open source project to safeguard agentic artificial intelligence and prevent cyber attacks.

Financial terms of the partnership weren't disclosed. The project, called Shirudo, helps protect running Linux systems without a reboot while teams roll out a patch.

With Shirudo, AI agents can find a vulnerability, build a shield and test that it stops the attack without disrupting the service, the companies said.

"So many teams rely on the same software that it makes sense to build these tools in the open," OpenAI Co-Founder Greg Brockman said. "Now when one team finds a better way to protect a system, others don't have to start from scratch."

Securities Class Action Filed Against MNTN, Inc. – MNTN Investors Encouraged to Contact Kirby McInerney LLP

The law firm of Kirby McInerney LLP announces that a class action lawsuit has been filed on behalf of investors who acquired MNTN, Inc. (“MNTN” or the “Company”) (NYSE: MNTN) securities between August 5, 2026 and November 4, 2026, inclusive (“the Class Period”). If you suffered a loss on your MNTN investments, you have until January 19, 2027 to request lead plaintiff appointment.

Investors are encouraged to fill out the contact form above or contact Lauren Molinaro of Kirby McInerney LLP by email at investigations@kmllp.com to discuss your rights or interests in the securities fraud class action lawsuit at no cost.

What Is This Lawsuit About? The lawsuit alleges that MNTN made false and/or misleading statements and failed to disclose that: (i) MNTN materially overstated the Company’s business prospects, considering that MNTN had instituted changes that caused many experienced salespeople to leave MNTN; and (ii) the foregoing materially impacted MNTN’s ability to meet its previously issued guidance for 2026.

On November 4, 2026, MNTN announced its third quarter 2026 financial results, reporting third quarter revenue of $80.3 million, below the Company’s previously stated guidance of $86 million to $89 million, and lowering its full year revenue guidance to a range of $311 million to $314 million, down from $347 million to $357 million. The Company also revealed that its Board of Directors had terminated the employment of MNTN CEO Mark Douglas and COO Christopher Innes, effective December 3, 2026 and December 1, 2026, respectively. Newly appointed CEO Tony Weisman explained the Company’s third quarter financial results, stating, “The company recently made significant changes in the sales team that did not work out, most notably a new compensation structure… They were implemented too quickly, resulting in sales force attrition. We lost about 40% of our experienced quota-carrying sellers, reducing our ability to bring in new business.” On this news, the price of MNTN shares declined by $5.67 per share, or approximately 54.67%, from $10.37 per share on November 4, 2026 to close at $4.70 on November 5, 2026.

Courts do not consider lead plaintiff applications submitted after the relevant deadline. If you choose to take no action, you may remain an absent class member. Learn more about the lead plaintiff process and eligibility requirements here. Courts typically appoint the investor(s) with the largest financial loss in the case and the ability to represent the class rather than investors with simply the largest investment portfolio. Courts regularly appoint individual investors, whether acting alone or as a group, as lead plaintiffs. The rights of any investor who bought shares during the class period are generally already protected. However, lead plaintiffs have the power to influence case strategy and have a say in settlement decisions, as well as decisions concerning allocation of settlement funds among class members.

data.title: U.S. stocks see best day in more than a year, as return of Jensen Huang revives AI enthusiasm
data.description:
By Christine Idzelis

Monday's session saw another 'V-shaped' rebound for stocks

The stock market saw a big rally Monday as investors appeared to celebrate Jensen Huang being reinstated as CEO at AI giant Nvidia.

Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia powered a massive bounce in the U.S. stock market on Monday by helping to restore faith in the artificial-intelligence trade.

The S&P 500 SPX surged 4.7% Monday, scoring its largest daily percentage gain since April 9, 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data. That marked a major shift in investor sentiment around AI, as investors appeared to cheer Huang's return in charge of the semiconductor giant at the center of the AI infrastructure buildout.

To be sure, the rebound was pretty broad-based, with stocks that aren't part of the AI theme tallying big gains as well. Nine of the S&P 500's 11 sectors finished higher Monday.

The entire stock market is behaving "a lot more like an individual security, with a lot of volatility and a lot of sensitivity" to the AI buildout, Kevin Khang, senior global economist at asset-management giant Vanguard, told MarketWatch in an interview Monday.

"The last six months is really the microcosm of what we should be expecting for the foreseeable future," at least for the next 12 months, said Khang. "Expect pretty high volatility and expect the source of the volatility to be something about the sustainability, or the future projected rate, of the AI buildout."

The U.S. stock market has been vulnerable to sudden mood changes around the AI trade, as investors keep reassessing the likelihood that the massive investment in AI infrastructure will yield a suitable return. The S&P 500 is top-heavy, with Big Tech stocks like Nvidia (NVDA) dominating the index, creating more opportunity for powerful swings.

The S&P 500's information-technology sector XX:SP500.45 soared 9% on Monday, as Nvidia's shares skyrocketed and chip stocks SOX broadly also surged, FactSet data showed.

Investors on Monday appeared to be "responding massively to Jensen being reinstated," Khang noted. Even before his reinstatement, however, stocks that had recently sold off amid an unwinding of the AI trade had "started to look very attractive" to some investors, he said.

Monday began with U.S. stock-market futures rallying, a rebound that accelerated ahead of the opening bell after news emerged that Huang was being reinstated as CEO, president and board member at Nvidia.

The Nasdaq Composite COMP soared more than 7% at the opening bell, its biggest gap higher at the open on record going back to 1991, Dow Jones Market Data showed.

Pressure on the U.S. stock market intensified after Huang resigned from Nvidia 11 days ago, adding to the headwinds facing the AI trade.

Check out: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia saved the stock market - for now. Will the rebound last?

But whether the pain is truly over remains to be seen. Wells Fargo Investment Institute's head of global investment strategy, Paul Christopher, cautioned against rushing into the stock market to make big bets in the market.

"We're not backing up the truck here" to buy stocks, Christopher said in a phone interview. "You could easily have another retest of 7,000" for the S&P 500 index, he noted.

At the root of the stock market's volatility is "who's going to win in AI," according to Christopher, and that is a question that will likely take time to answer.

The Cboe Volatility Index VIX finished Monday at 26.62, down nearly 26%.

The S&P 500 closed Monday at about 7,237. That's after ending Friday at 6910.39, following a brutal drop last week that saw it enter a correction along with Dow Jones Jones Industrial Average DJIA. The tech-heavy Nasdaq, which had entered a correction earlier in November, saw an ugly drop Friday that wiped out its 2026 gains - though its bounce Monday put it back into the green for the year.

-Christine Idzelis

Net cash provided by operating activities was driven by strong cash earnings, disciplined working capital management, and reflects one less pay cycle compared to the prior year quarter. Net cash used in investing activities included $22 million in capital expenditures. Net cash used in financing activities consisted primarily of $287 million in voluntary principal payment on the Term Loan B. As of October 2, 2026, Amentum had $521 million in cash and cash equivalents and $3,574 million of gross debt. With net leverage reduced to 2.7x, Amentum has strengthened its financial position, providing greater flexibility for disciplined and opportunistic deployment.

Share Repurchase Authorization

Subsequent to quarter end, the Company’s Board of Directors authorized the repurchase of up to $500 million of the Company’s common stock. The share repurchase program provides additional flexibility to deploy capital as part of the Company’s disciplined capital allocation strategy.

Backlog and Contract Awards

As of October 2, 2026, the Company had total backlog of $48.3 billion, which includes an approximately $1.5 billion de-booking related to contract changes at NASA, compared with $47.1 billion as of October 3, 2025, an increase of 2.4% driven by $15.0 billion in net bookings and 1.1x book-to-bill. Funded backlog as of October 2, 2026 was $6.0 billion, compared with $5.6 billion as of October 3, 2025, an increase of 8.0%.

  • NGA Integrated Campus Support (NICS) – The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) awarded Amentum an $800 million ten-year contract to deliver technology-enabled solutions that maximize the performance of critical facilities and systems at NGA Washington. The award builds on Amentum’s successful track record of supporting critical infrastructure for national security missions at NGA and across the U.S. government and its allies across the globe.
  • Navy Integrated Training Environment (NITE) 2 – The U.S. Navy awarded Amentum a new $700 million five-year contract to provide comprehensive operations and engineering solutions for the Navy’s live, virtual, and constructive integrated environment. Under this contract, Amentum will use secure AI and data analytics to enhance maintenance and operations, improve system readiness, and modernize systems for complex training scenarios.
  • Australia Nuclear Submarine Shipyard Program – The Australian Naval Infrastructure (ANI) selected an Amentum-led joint venture as its Capability Partner to support the delivery of a nuclear-powered submarine construction yard in South Australia, providing program and construction management. This ten-year program reinforces Amentum’s position as a trusted industry partner, leveraging its extensive global nuclear experience in waterfront infrastructure, waste management, and regulatory in support of supporting global nuclear capabilities.
  • U.S. Army Germany Site Operations – The U.S. Army awarded Amentum a new $375 million single-award indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity contract with a six-year ordering period to strengthen U.S. Army mission readiness across 21 installations in Germany. Through this award, Amentum will leverage its global expertise and advanced digital solutions to enhance operational efficiency, modernize installation support, and enable mission-critical operations.

Amentum will support spent fuel management and retrievals mission through its full lifecycle capabilities, including engineering and design, installation, plant modification, project management and ongoing asset care. Formal award of the framework agreement will follow when final contractual arrangements are concluded.
  • Navy Counter-Unmanned Systems (C-UxS) – The U.S. Navy awarded Amentum a $145 million single-award indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity contract with a five-year ordering period to support the U.S. Navy’s modernization of advanced counter-unmanned systems through research, development, testing, and integration of next-generation technologies to enhance operational capabilities.

The presentation and discussion of Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA Margin, Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted Diluted EPS, Free Cash Flow, and Net Leverage are not measures of financial performance under Generally Accepted Accounting Principles in the United States (“GAAP”). These non-GAAP measures should be considered only as supplements to, and should not be considered in isolation or used as a substitute for, financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP. Management believes these non-GAAP measures, when read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP and the reconciliations herein to the most directly comparable GAAP measures, provide useful information in assessing trends in our ongoing operating performance and may provide greater visibility in understanding the long-term financial performance of the Company. The computation of non-GAAP measures may not be comparable to similarly titled measures reported by other companies, thus limiting their use for comparability.

Adjusted EBITDA is defined as GAAP net income attributable to common shareholders adjusted for interest expense and other, net, provision for income taxes, depreciation and amortization, and excludes the following discrete items:

  • Acquisition, transaction, and integration costs – Represents acquisition, transaction and integration costs, including severance, retention, and other adjustments related to acquisition and integration activities.
  • Amortization of intangibles – Represents the amortization of intangible assets.
  • Divestitures – Represents divestiture gains and losses.
  • Loss on extinguishment of debt – Represents the write-off of debt discount and debt issuance costs as a result of debt modifications.
  • Utilization of certain fair market value adjustments assigned in purchase accounting – Represents the periodic utilization of the fair market value adjustments assigned to certain equity method investments and non-controlling interests based on the remaining period of performance for the related contract.
  • Stock-based compensation – Represents non-cash compensation expenses recognized for stock-based arrangements.

Adjusted EBITDA Margin is defined as Adjusted EBITDA divided by revenues.

Adjusted Net Income is defined as GAAP net income attributable to common shareholders excluding the discrete items listed under Adjusted EBITDA and the related tax impacts.

Adjusted Diluted EPS is defined as Adjusted Net Income divided by diluted weighted average number of common shares outstanding.

Free Cash Flow is defined as GAAP cash flow provided by operating activities less purchases of property and equipment. For fiscal year 2026, Free Cash Flow was $583 million, consisting of $627 million of GAAP cash flow provided by operating activities less $44 million of purchases of property and equipment.

Net Leverage is defined as GAAP total debt (excluding unamortized original issue discount and deferred financing costs) less cash and cash equivalents, divided by last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA, which is a non-GAAP measure. For fiscal year 2026, Net Leverage was 2.7x, consisting of $3,574 million of total debt less $521 million of cash and cash equivalents, divided by the last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA of $1,132 million.

data.title: Amazon may have just found a 'cheap' way to get a lot more out of its chips
data.description:
By Emily Bary

Amazon's deal for Decart's AI technology, with a reported price of $7.5 billion, may be a relatively inexpensive way to boost the speed and efficiency of its custom chips, says an analyst

Amazon's newly disclosed deal could help increase AWS's capacity, according to an analyst.

While certainty not the biggest semiconductor-related news of the day, Amazon.com just made a move that analysts say could enhance the performance of the company's custom chips.

Amazon (AMZN) announced on Monday morning that it has purchased artificial-intelligence optimization technology from Decart, an AI research lab founded in 2023.

The Decart technology "will help Amazon further optimize both its inference and custom silicon performance so more customers can train and run AI models faster and at lower cost," the e-commerce giant said in a statement.

"Everything humanity is about to build runs on a limited number of chips," Decart's website said. "The future depends on extracting far more performance from the compute we already have."

Terms of the deal weren't disclosed, though Bloomberg News put the price at around $7.5 billion. Amazon and Decart didn't immediately respond to a MarketWatch request for comment.

Don't miss: Microsoft is winning the cloud wars and becoming Wall Street's new golden child

"We view the deal as strategically sensible and financially manageable," Evercore ISI analyst Mark Mahaney said in a note to clients. "The payoff is incremental AWS capacity: Software that gets more useful work out of each chip effectively adds sellable compute without requiring an equivalent increase" in spending on chips, power or other data-center hardware.

Amazon disclosed in its statement that Decart AI co-founders Dean Leitersdorf, Moshe Shalev and Orian Leitersdorf, as well as their team of engineers and research staffers, will be joining the company.

"While the headline price appears full for a 100-person startup," Mahaney noted that the rumored price represents about 0.3% of Amazon's market capitalization. In that sense, "this may be a cheap option on making Trainium faster and cheaper to run."

Trainium is Amazon's line of custom chips, which Mahaney said is growing at a triple-digit rate already, with soaring revenue commitments. The company has plans to start selling Trainium chips outside of its AWS cloud-computing business next year.

Amazon shares rose 3.5% on Monday amid a broad-based surge in technology stocks fueled by Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia.

-Emily Bary

data.title: Short sellers get smoked as Nvidia tallies biggest one-day gain in stock-market history
data.description:
By Joseph Adinolfi

Two products aiming to profit off daily declines in Nvidia shares were nearly wiped out as the stock rallied more than 30%

The Nvidia board has reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO following pressure from the White House.

Short sellers who bet against Nvidia got clobbered on Monday as the stock soared more than 30%, causing its market capitalization to increase by $950 billion - the biggest single-day gain for any stock in the history of the U.S. market.

Nvidia (NVDA) shares closed at $165.05, up $39.52, or 31.5%. For short sellers who had borrowed Nvidia shares and sold them on the hope they could later buy them back more cheaply and pocket the difference, that amount to a loss of about $11.2 billion - the biggest one-day loss for Nvidia shorts going back to 2019, according to data from Peter Hillerberg, co-founder of ORTEX, which monitors short-sellers' losses.

Monday's losses more than wiped out short sellers' profits from last week, although they're still up by about $15 billion since Oct. 29, Hillerberg said.

"Nvidia short sellers lost about $11.2 billion on paper today, more than twice their previous worst day in our data going back to 2019," Hillerberg told MarketWatch on Monday.

In London, two leveraged exchange-traded products that aimed to capture minus three times the daily moves in Nvidia were nearly wiped out as the shares rallied by more than 30%, according to FactSet data.

The Leverage Shares -3x short Nvidia ETP fell by more than 80% in a matter of minutes after the opening bell, FactSet data showed.

A separate product from GraniteShares, which also advertises minus three times the daily move in Nvidia shares, fell by 92%.

Stop-loss measures embedded in both products helped to stave off a liquidation, according to representatives from Leverage Shares and GraniteShares.

Still, Monday's episode offered investors another uncomfortable reminder of an incident that took place on Feb. 5, 2018. On that day, the Cboe Volatility Index VIX, known as Wall Street's "fear gauge," doubled - wiping out popular short-volatility products in an incident remembered on Wall Street as "Volmageddon."

"Whether it's terminated or it rebalances, it doesn't change the fact that you just went down 90%," said Eric Balchunas, senior ETF strategist at Bloomberg Intelligence, in a conversation with MarketWatch. "This is a wipeout - if you were in one of these, you just lost everything."

Other popular inverse Nvidia products traded in the U.S. and elsewhere in Europe also tallied their biggest losses on record. Nvidia hasn't seen such a large daily gain since 2003, long before these products were launched, Dow Jones Market Data showed.

At the same time, leveraged long Nvidia products, including several trading in the U.S., were on track for their biggest daily gains on record.

The GraniteShares 2x Long NVDA Daily ETF NVDL was skyrocketing around 62% on Monday afternoon. By contrast, the GraniteShares 2x Short NVDA Daily ETF NVD was plunging around 63% in Monday afternoon trading, FactSet data showed, at last check.

Leveraged exchange-traded products, particularly those that track the performance of a single stock, are intended to be used for intraday trading. Because of how they're designed, volatility drag often weighs on performance over time, regardless of which direction the underlying stock is moving.

For example, GraniteShares' NVDL and NVD products are both sitting on year-to-date losses of more than 40% as of Monday afternoon, according to FactSet. Meanwhile, Nvidia is down a little over 11% since the start of the year through Monday.

The Nvidia board voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday, according to a statement. Media reports revealed that the board faced pressure from the White House to bring back Huang, who had resigned 11 days prior after admitting to several affairs, including with Nvidia employees and a suspected Chinese spy.

Christine Idzelis and Michael DeStefano contributed.

data.title: Welgemda™ (BBP-418, Ribitol) Receives Traditional Approval as the First and Only Treatment for Individuals Living with LGMD2I/R9
data.description:
- Welgemda is the first and only FDA-approved therapy for individuals living with LGMD2I/R9 (FKRP-related), and represents the first approved treatment for any form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy

- FDA granted traditional approval to Welgemda based on positive Phase 3 FORTIFY results: a 0.27 m/s benefit versus placebo on 100MTT velocity and 4.89% benefit versus placebo on FVC percent predicted at 12 months; and a nominally significant improvement on NSAD, a measure of motor performance in ambulatory and non-ambulatory patients, versus a decline with placebo

- BridgeBio anticipates an immediate U.S. launch and is committed to helping eligible individuals access Welgemda through its patient support program, ForgingBridges®, which includes insurance resources, financial assistance options, and a dedicated support team to assist at every stage of the diagnosis and treatment journey

- With this approval, the FDA also issued a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher

- Management remarks video on FDA approval available

PALO ALTO, Calif., Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. (Nasdaq: BBIO) (“BridgeBio” or the “Company”), a commercial-stage, multi-product biopharmaceutical company focused on developing medicines for genetic conditions, today announced that the FDA granted traditional (full) approval to Welgemda™ (BBP-418, ribitol), an oral small molecule, for the treatment of adult and pediatric individuals living with limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9) (FKRP-related) weighing at least 30 kg. The approval is based on positive clinical data from FORTIFY, the Phase 3 clinical trial of Welgemda in individuals with LGMD2I/R9. With this approval, the FDA also issued a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher.

"This is a transformative moment for the LGMD2I/R9 community, with the first and only treatment now approved for this chronic, progressive disease,” said Christine Siu, Chief Executive Officer of BridgeBio Neuromuscular. “We are grateful to the community, the trial participants and their families, our investigators, and patient advocates, and the FDA review team, who have all worked tirelessly with our team to accomplish this milestone. Welgemda has demonstrated the potential to be a disease-modifying treatment with clinically meaningful and statistically significant benefit observed across all key endpoints, and exploratory analyses showed a consistent benefit across all prespecified subgroups. We are committed to making Welgemda available to as many patients as possible as quickly as possible.”

In the Phase 3 FORTIFY trial, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, Welgemda met its primary and key secondary endpoints at the 12-month interim analysis. On the 100-meter timed test (100MTT), a measure of ambulatory ability, individuals treated with Welgemda showed a 0.27 m/s benefit in velocity relative to placebo at 12 months (p<0.0001). Forced vital capacity (FVC), a measure of pulmonary function, improved approximately 3% from baseline in individuals treated with Welgemda and declined approximately 2% in the placebo group, a treatment benefit of roughly 5% at 12 months (p=0.0071). Welgemda also demonstrated a nominally significant improvement from baseline, compared to a decline in the placebo arm, on the North Star Assessment for Limb Girdle Muscular Dystrophies (NSAD), a composite scale measuring motor performance in both ambulatory and non-ambulatory individuals. Consistent with its proposed mechanism of action, individuals treated with Welgemda also showed a rapid and sustained increase in alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation observed at 3 months (p<0.0001) and sustained at 12 months (p<0.0001) and a substantial reduction in serum creatine kinase (CK) at 12 months (p<0.0001). Welgemda was generally well tolerated. The most common adverse reaction was diarrhea, with no serious cases reported, and there were no discontinuations due to adverse reactions associated with Welgemda.

“When I was 5 years old, I learned that I had LGMD2I/R9. After my diagnosis, my mom founded the CureLGMD2i Foundation, and for 15 years, my family along with others across the community have devoted tireless effort, made countless sacrifices, and persevered to bring a treatment forward, so this approval is incredibly meaningful,” said Sammy Brazzo, an individual living with LGMD2I/R9 and intern at CureLGMD2i Foundation. “Most importantly, it also means hope for people living with LGMD2I/R9 and for families facing this diagnosis today and in the future. Our community has worked toward a moment like this, driven by the belief that a better future was possible. Knowing that people may now have an option that did not exist before makes every late night, every fundraiser, every meeting, and every setback worth it.”

With FDA approval, BridgeBio will transition all active U.S. FORTIFY participants, including those randomized to placebo during the double-blind period, into the ongoing FORTIFY open-label extension (OLE), through which they will receive Welgemda. Trial sites outside the U.S. will continue the study as planned until each participant completes 36 months of treatment. Welgemda is not yet approved or available in any market outside of the U.S. and continued participation in the study will support generation of the data needed to support regulatory approval and access in territories outside of the U.S.

"Families living with LGMD2I/R9 have never had disease specific treatment and only had supportive care to manage progression," said Matthew Wicklund, M.D., FAAN, Professor of Neurology and Vice Chair for Research, Department of Neurology at the University of Texas (UT) Health Science Center San Antonio. "What we saw in FORTIFY was different: individuals became measurably better at the things that matter most day to day, including breathing easier, walking faster, walking farther, and less fatigue. This is the first time any therapy has shown this kind of functional improvement in LGMD2I/R9, and certainly a first in the limb girdle muscular dystrophies. I am thrilled by what this approval means for the community. For a relentlessly progressive disease, the ability to regain function, rather than simply lose it more slowly, is what will let people hold onto their mobility, their independence, and their quality of life for longer."

BridgeBio anticipates an immediate U.S. launch of Welgemda. As part of ensuring individuals with LGMD2I/R9 can access Welgemda as quickly as possible, the Company offers a patient support services program, ForgingBridges®, for individuals in the U.S. prescribed Welgemda and their families, including insurance resources, financial assistance options, and a dedicated support team to assist at every stage of the diagnosis and treatment journey.

BridgeBio intends to submit a Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) to the European Medicines Agency (EMA) in the first half of 2028. The MAA will be based on the final analysis of the Phase 3 FORTIFY study at Month 36, with topline results expected late 2027/early 2028. The Company intends to initiate clinical studies of BBP-418 in LGMD2I/R9 for individuals who are less than 12 years of age weighing less than 30 kg in the first half of 2027, as well as in LGMD2M/R13 and in LGMD2U/R20 in the near future.

Welgemda is indicated for the treatment of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9) in adult and pediatric patients weighing at least 30 kg.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION
What are the possible side effects of Welgemda?
The most common side effects of Welgemda include: diarrhea, stomach pain, nausea, joint pain, indigestion or heartburn, flu, and passing gas. There were no severe or serious cases of diarrhea reported. If you experience
persistent or worsening diarrhea, tell your healthcare provider.

These are not all of the possible side effects of Welgemda.

In the clinical study, no one stopped taking Welgemda because of side effects.

About Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9)
LGMD2I/R9 (FKRP-related) is a monogenic autosomal recessive disease caused by partial loss of function mutations in the fukutin-related protein (FKRP) gene, and FKRP mutations impair glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan (αDG), a protein associated with stabilizing muscle cells. Clinical manifestations typically present as a skeletal myopathy affecting the lower and then upper limbs, which is commonly later accompanied by pulmonary muscle and cardiac muscle involvement. Individuals who harbor a homozygous L276I genotype typically develop disease manifestations during late childhood with progression to loss of independent ambulation (25%), assisted ventilation (10%), and cardiomyopathy (30%) in adulthood. Cardiomyopathy is progressive, with an annual loss of 0.4% of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Individuals with other FKRP genotypes typically have an earlier childhood onset with a more severe clinical course, rapid loss of mobility by 20 years of age, more frequent cardiac involvement (60%), and eventual pulmonary decline by 30 years of age in nearly all cases. Approximately 7,000 individuals currently live with LGMD2I/R9 and other addressable α-dystroglycanopathies in the U.S. and Europe.
